scenarios.name: theory-grounding
scenarios.input: Fetch https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch_sphere with http_fetch. Then state the standard relation between a qubit state |psi> = alpha|0> + beta|1> and the Bloch sphere angles theta and phi.

scenarios.name: theory-normalization
scenarios.input: For a pure qubit state, |alpha|^2 + |beta|^2 = 1. If |alpha|^2 = 0.25, use the calculator to compute |beta|^2 exactly and state it.

scenarios.name: theory-born-rule
scenarios.input: Explain in one paragraph why |alpha|^2 + |beta|^2 = 1 for a qubit, and what each term means physically.

judge.rubric: The answer must explain that probabilities must sum to 1 (normalization / Born rule) and that |alpha|^2 and |beta|^2 are the probabilities of measuring 0 and 1.

scenarios.name: engineer-html-fence
scenarios.input: Write a complete, minimal single-file HTML page that draws a circle on a <canvas>. Put the full HTML inside a ```html fenced block and nothing else outside the fence.

scenarios.name: engineer-hadamard-math
scenarios.input: The Hadamard gate maps |0> to (|0>+|1>)/sqrt(2). Use the calculator to verify that (1/sqrt(2))^2 = 0.5 and state the two probabilities.

scenarios.name: reviewer-catch-x
scenarios.input: A colleague implemented the X gate and claims that applying X to |0> leaves the state with P(0)=0.5. Use the calculator to check the claim (X|0> = |1> so P(1)=1). Is the colleague right?

judge.rubric: The answer must conclude the colleague is wrong and state that after X|0> the state is |1> with P(1)=1.

scenarios.name: reviewer-arrow-bug
scenarios.input: A Bloch sphere demo renders the initial |0> state with an arrow of zero length at the center of the sphere. Give a verdict: is the visualization correct?

judge.rubric: The answer must say the visualization is buggy: |0> is the north pole and the arrow must have full length pointing up.

scenarios.name: analyst-decides-mitigation
scenarios.input: Execution report from a real run of a Bell-state experiment: ideal counts {'00': 2009, '11': 2087}; noisy counts {'00': 1824, '11': 1881, '01': 198, '10': 193}; fidelity 0.9045; error rate 0.0955. Decision rule: fidelity below 0.95 requires error mitigation. Give your verdict and the concrete mitigation you would request.

judge.rubric: The answer must conclude MITIGATION REQUIRED (fidelity 0.9045 < 0.95), report the error rate ~0.0955, and propose readout calibration + correction (assignment matrix / least squares) as the mitigation.

scenarios.name: analyst-verdict-compare
scenarios.input: Two real runs of the same Bell-state experiment with the same noise model: RUN 1 (raw) fidelity 0.9045, error rate 0.0955. RUN 2 (with readout error mitigation) fidelity 0.9808, mitigated error rate 0.0192. State both numbers, the delta, whether mitigation was effective, and the final verdict (ACCEPTABLE or FURTHER MITIGATION NEEDED).

judge.rubric: The answer must state both fidelities (0.9045 and 0.9808) or equivalent and the delta (+0.076), conclude mitigation improved fidelity, and give a verdict of ACCEPTABLE (or justify FURTHER MITIGATION NEEDED with the remaining gate error).
